claims.claim: Discord's privileged-intent threshold is 10,000 unique users, with annual reapplication; verification and intent review are separate processes.
Discord's channel-obfuscation change is scheduled for 2026-11-16: hidden channels are omitted from HTTP and arrive on the gateway with the CHANNEL_OBFUSCATED flag and a null/placeholder name.
Components V2 allows at most 40 components per message; the flag is irreversible and defer-then-edit is required for a V2 response.
Components V2 combines text across text-bearing components into a roughly 4,000-character budget.
An application may register 100 global chat-input commands, 15 user-context commands, 15 message-context commands and one primary entry point.
Native AutoMod allows 6 keyword rules and 10 regex patterns per guild, with 260-character Rust-flavour regexes.
A bot must shard at 2,500 guilds, with a maximum of 2,500 guilds per shard, and must not hardcode shard counts.
If an app is monetized anywhere, Discord's Premium Apps rules require an equivalent in-Discord purchase at a price no higher than the other channel (effective 2024-10-07).
No surveyed generalist documents a complete export of its own config and history; portability exists because destination bots implement pull or file import.
MEE6 levels can be read from its public leaderboard and are imported by Lurkr, Atom and Cakey; MEE6 publishes no documented official API.
Dyno documents no public API or server-config export; Carl-bot documents no general export (tags are a narrow exception); Wick documents no API.
Ticket Tool does not store transcripts server-side; it generates an HTML file and sends it as a Discord message, so the user must archive it before deleting the ticket.
ProBot's ticket module can deliver transcripts as HTML, JSON or plain text to a transcript channel, making JSON the most portable surveyed format.
Paid single-server all-in-one tiers cluster around $3.50-$8/month; MEE6 is an outlier near $12/month; per-server billing is a common switching trigger.
Paid tiers most often sell multiples, a faster/private shard, white-label identity, integrations, retention and API access rather than unique core features.
Red-DiscordBot's cog registry, YAGPDB's bot/web/feed process split and TSCord's declarative guards are the strongest open-source patterns for a modular, self-hostable bot.

Skyra tells users not to self-host, NadekoBot requires a copyright-assigning CLA, and Auttaja's Kubernetes-only architecture outlived its maintainers; each is a contributor or bus-factor failure mode.
Discord's production OAuth2 flow is authorization code with PKCE; state must be bound to the pre-login session and iss validated; implicit grant is not recommended.
Per-guild authorization needs both the user's guild permissions (BigInt MANAGE_GUILD/ADMINISTRATOR) and a bot-token check that the bot is in the guild; a :guildId URL must never be trusted alone.
The most repeated owner complaints are retroactive paywalls, bot sprawl, per-server billing, dashboard/command parity bugs and context-blind automod; AI persona marketing draws visible distrust.

MEE6 Premium lists $11.99/month, $49.99/year or $89.99 lifetime for a single server; the free plan caps reaction roles at 40 and leaves most moderation, automations and leveling behind Premium, while MEE6 AI is sold separately.

Dyno's free plan includes 19 automod filters, moderation, one reaction-role menu, three giveaways, tickets and starboard; Standard is $5.99/month, Premium $7.99 and Custom $12.99 per server, with levels and social integrations on paid plans.

Carl-bot gives 250 reaction roles, 5 YouTube and 2 Twitch alerts and 100 weblog entries free; Premium raises those to 1,000 / 20 / 5 / 500 and adds levels, sticky messages, autopurge, voice-role links, timed roles and Drama Watcher, sold at $7.99, $12.99 or $16.99 per month for 1, 2 or 3 server slots.

ProBot's free plan covers welcome images, logs, moderation, autoroles, starboard, reaction roles and invites; Tier 1 is $5/month, Tier 2 is $10/month per server, and Tier 2 adds anti-raid and a custom bot identity.

Arcane's free tier has message and reaction XP, 15 role rewards and weekly leaderboards; voice XP, custom XP values, custom rank cards, unlimited role rewards and hourly first-place refresh need the $7/month or $75/year Premium and a premium bot invite.

Lurkr keeps every feature free forever and sells only higher limits: $5/month Ultimate raises role rewards from 3 to 10 per level, the total from 50 to 100 and the leaderboard from 100 to 500 users; the free tier includes MEE6 import and a public API.

Ticket Tool's free plan includes unlimited tickets, three panels, five live flows, transcripts and a knowledge base with 30-day history; Community is $5/month and Pro $12/month adds autonomous AI, API and webhook nodes, 12-month retention, SLA and CSAT reports, and a custom KB domain.

Helper.gg's free plan has unlimited tickets, replies from its web panel, staff accounts, ticket logs and AI replies; Premium is $4.90/month for translation, automation and customization, and a further $3.90/month adds a custom bot identity.

Wick keeps core anti-nuke, anti-raid, heat automod, quarantine, lockdown and restore free; its $5/month Premium adds advanced variants, smart backups and panic mode, and $20/month VIP covers 12 servers with branding and lower latency, according to a third-party price check of Wick's own premium page.

Double Counter's free plan covers alt detection, raid and VPN/Tor blocking, three verification modes and more than 20 settings; Pro adds ad-free verification, custom embeds and timeouts, device-fingerprint analytics, cross-database checks and right-click actions, billed inside Discord.

Statbot's free plan covers message, voice and member statistics with a 30-day lookback, four Statroles and eight Statdock counter types; History, Data+, Drilldowns, Statdocks+ and Statroles+ are sold as bundles from $8.97 to $14.95/month, and API access requires every upgrade.

Jockie Music plays across multiple bot instances and keeps 50 collections per person free; Patreon boosts unlock audio filters at 2 boosts, 24/7 mode and an extra bot at 5 boosts, and collections rise to 200 with premium.

Apollo's free plan has unlimited events, one active recurring event, one reminder and capacity with an automatic waitlist; Premium is $8/month for unlimited recurring events, five reminders, restricted events, attendee roles and automatic Google Calendar sync, and Pro is $25/month.

GiveawayBot's public command list covers button entry, /gstart, /gend, /gdelete, /glist and /greroll plus a right-click reroll; premium is donation-based and its feature list is not published, so entry requirements and analytics are not claimed.

UnbelievaBoat's free economy includes a 25-item shop with two actions and two requirements, games, moderation and 25-message logs; Premium removes the item limit, allows five actions and requirements, adds ten custom income commands, a custom profile, 30% off role income and 100-message logs.

PeakBot advertises 30+ features free and sells Starter at $4/month and Pro at $8.25/month or $69/year per server; Pro adds the AI Server Builder, text-and-image AI moderation, AI analytics and 25 daily backups.

YourBot runs ten services on a shared bot for free and charges $4.99/month or $47.85/year per server for Premium, which adds a custom bot, the plugin marketplace, the Plugin Builder and 50 server designs; AI builds are paid from prepaid credits and the platform is still beta.

Wallu sells knowledge-base AI support from $4.99/month per account with 350 AI responses and nine channels, including ticket automation, voice answers and a strict mode that stays silent when its documents do not cover a question; it documents a 7-day trial, not a permanent free tier.
MEE6's wiki states that Manage Server is enough to invite the bot but not to see the dashboard: you must have Administrator or be the server owner.

MEE6's free-vs-premium comparison marks Reaction Role, Welcome & Goodbye and XP and Levels as unavailable on Free, and lists Moderation in the same gated table; the page states current gating only and does not say those features were formerly free.
Dyno's module docs present 33 module cards across six categories and a dashboard where manager roles grant access; Dyno publishes no advertised total module count.

Carl-bot GitHub issue #50 ('Reaction roles on the website doesn't work') has been open since 2022-06-30; its newest comment, on 2025-12-15, says 'Every time I click save, nothing happens,' and no comment continues into 2026.

Ticket Tool's current docs configure panels through in-dashboard channel and category pickers and require Administrator to edit configuration; no page read mentions Developer Mode, so the 'raw ids' critique does not hold for its 2026 dashboard.
ProBot's dashboard docs require Administrator permission to see a server: 'You need Administrator permission to see your server on the list.'
Wick's dashboard overview gives a list of issues to fix, and its setup wizard accepts a channel mention, name or id rather than requiring a raw snowflake.
Statbot never deletes data but free users can view at most 30 days back (14 days by default), and tracking begins at invite time rather than retroactively.
